title: Phase D mock-ups — attachment chips and the terminal's backing
_note: Nothing here ships. The chip designs live on a workbench-only page; the terminal variants are a workbench-only switch over a frozen sample screen. Yes = 'this one is acceptable', No = 'not this one', Other = say what you'd change.

steps.headline: A: one-line chips — type icon, name cut after 16 letters (full name on hover), ✕ always visible. No preview.
steps.changed: The cheapest fix: the 48 px squares become 28 px pills. Same row at desktop and at phone width underneath.
steps.measured: 28 px tall; 6 of 11 files fit before the row scrolls at desktop width
steps.notice: Every name is readable and every ✕ is there without hovering. You never see what is inside a file.
steps.risk: No picture thumbnails at all — a step down from today for images.

steps.path: Design B — card with a name strip
steps.headline: B: 96×72 cards — a preview on top, the name in an 11 px strip along the bottom, ✕ always visible.
steps.changed: Your direction. Pictures show a thumbnail; markdown, text and code show their first lines; everything else shows a big type glyph with the extension (PDF, XLSX, MP3, MP4, ZIP…).
steps.measured: 96 × 72 px; text previews are 9 px — the sample lines are canned, the real version would read the file's first few lines
steps.notice: You can tell files apart at a glance and read most names in full. The row is taller than today (72 px vs 48) so the composer grows a little while files are attached.
steps.risk: The ✕ sits over the first line of a text preview; the 9 px preview text is a texture, not something to read.

steps.headline: C: the same card at 128×96 so the text preview is actually readable; name strip at 12 px.
steps.changed: B scaled up one step. Same previews per file kind.
steps.measured: 128 × 96 px; 10 px preview text; only 3 cards fit at phone width before scrolling
steps.notice: Previews become legible and names almost never truncate, but the attachment row takes twice today's height and the composer pushes the chat up noticeably.
steps.risk: At phone width three cards fill the row — anything past that is a sideways scroll.

steps.path: Terminal → wallpaper theme → as it is today
steps.headline: Today, for reference: the terminal text is drawn at 60% opacity straight over the blurred wallpaper.
steps.changed: Nothing — this is the current look, shown on a frozen sample screen so the three wallpaper/flat themes can be compared. Midnight is the flat-theme reference: identical in every variant.
steps.measured: Text at 60% opacity over the wallpaper (the theme's default)
steps.notice: Use this step to anchor the next three; answer Yes here only if you want no change at all.
steps.risk: The sample screen is canned Claude Code output, not a live session.

steps.headline: Scrim: the same wallpaper look, but the terminal is drawn at 85% instead of 60%.
steps.changed: Only the opacity changes. The wallpaper still shows through, less strongly.
steps.notice: Text is noticeably darker/brighter and easier to read; the theme still feels like itself.
steps.risk: Under a busy wallpaper (Halftone) the pattern still competes with small text.

steps.headline: Solid 90%: the terminal sits on the theme's panel colour at 90%, the same guarantee the chat panels have.
steps.changed: The terminal's backing becomes the panel colour, 90% opaque; a hint of wallpaper remains. The strip above the terminal is unchanged in every variant.
steps.notice: Terminal text reads like chat text does over wallpapers; you lose most of the wallpaper inside the terminal area but keep it around it.
steps.risk: Meadow Mist's own hand-made terminal backdrop is replaced by the flat panel colour.

steps.headline: Solid 100%: a fully opaque panel — no wallpaper inside the terminal at all.
steps.changed: Same as the 90% version, fully opaque.
steps.notice: Maximum readability; inside the terminal the theme looks like a flat theme.
steps.risk: Wallpaper packs lose their character in Terminal view.
